utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is the case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we continue, the Chamber would like to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Witness JF-005, first of all, I would like to remind you that the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony is still binding upon you. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is clear. Then, Mr. Jordash, are you ready to continue your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. If I could have a moment to just move along the bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: When Stankovic ordered you to join the MP unit, he also ordered the remainder of your unit to join the Ozren Guard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And we were reassigned to other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So other members of your unit were assigned by Stankovic to other units; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We asked him to reassign us to other units. We asked for that to be done. We had a conversation with him, where we asked to be reassigned to other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And he was responsible for assigning everybody to those other units; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my case, it is correct. As for the others, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. After the assignment -- after your assignment, Djuro Martic gave you orders in relation to liberating the corridor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. But other members were present as well, other members of the unit that was at Ozren during the breach or the breakthrough of the corridor in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And they were receiving orders from Djuro Martic as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, depending on the group where -- to which they belonged, there would be other -- there would be various individuals who would be responsible. So there wasn't just one responsible person, because there were a number of units who were stationed there, not just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And these units were all under the Ozren Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, they were subordinated to Colonel Novica Simic - I think he was a colonel at the time - and he was in charge of Operation Corridor, and there were a few other officers who were in charge of this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Were they -- all these officers you mentioned were part of the Tactical Group Ozren?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were part of Tactical Group Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And that was ultimately under the command of Stankovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I was clear enough. I said that Major Stankovic was the commander of the Tactical Group Ozren, and within the group itself, Novica Simic was the person in charge. I think I was pretty clear on that in my previous statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry to labour the point. Maybe you were clear. I just want to make sure I'm clear. Stankovic, then, is the top commander of these units that you describe. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there -- we should mention the units that were there. There were four Ozren brigades that were under the direct command of Stankovic. There were three other brigades that were near Doboj and they were subordinated directly to the Tactical Group Doboj. Again, we're talking about May 1992, and about the entry into Doboj, in charge of which was Bozovic, together with all the groups that had come from other -- from elsewhere. So I can't say exactly what was going on, because I was not in the command or operation centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, who was in commander of the Tactical Group Doboj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, I believe it was Novica Simic at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And he answered to Stankovic. He took --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He probably answered to the General Staff. But here I'm referring to another period, the second half of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, let's deal with the first half. Did Simic answer to Stankovic in the first half?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no information to say either way.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: He was a member of JNA or -- or a TO; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, I believe he was a JNA member, but I'm not certain. I think he was a member of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. When you were in charge of -- sorry. When -- when -- no, I think I don't need to ask that. When you were working with the 1st Motorised Brigade you took orders directly from Mladic; is that right? The 1st Motorised Brigade, I should have said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not work with the 1st Motorised Brigade. I was a member of the 1st Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you take your orders from Mladic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We did not take our orders from Mladic. We took our orders from Colonel Lazic, who was the commander of the 1st Guards Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And did Lazic take his orders from Mladic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 1st Guards Motorised Brigade was under the direct command of the General Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Which was commanded ultimately by Mladic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And after you completed your work with the 1st Guards Motorised Brigade, you joined the Doboj Brigade, which was a unit of the VRS; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you took your orders from which VRS person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't recall at this point what the commander's name was. But we had -- I'm sorry, I can't -- I'm just -- I can't recall right now. I apologise. If I do remember -- recall the name, I will tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. The Tactical Group Ozren had another name before becoming known as the Tactical Group Ozren. Can you recall what that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't recall. 17 years have elapsed. It's a lot of time, and it's hard to remember every little detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you recall that it did have a name before becoming the Tactical Group Ozren? It existed and had another name; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a name for it, but I can't recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And did it consist of JNA unit along with TO unit before it became known as the Tactical Group Ozren?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's possible. But, as I said, I can't really remember the name exactly. I can tell you what I know, but I can't tell you what I don't, and I can't really claim or ascertain if I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can you confirm, though, it was under the command of Stankovic before becoming the Tactical Group Ozren, or before becoming known as the Tactical Group Ozren?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And when it became the Tactical Group Ozren, it then, as you've told us, it remained under Stankovic's command.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, I want to refer you back now to evidence you gave on Thursday last, and you told the Court that when you were in the JSN, Dragan Lukic was in charge of the JSN? Am I quoting your evidence correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You also confirmed, on Thursday last, that Dragan Lukic was directly subordinated to the Ozren Tactical Group at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And when the various groups, military groups, including the JSN entered Doboj on the 3rd of May, everyone was under that command, the Ozren Tactical Group. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they had a forward command post in Lipac.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And who was in command there; do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I did not take orders from them at the time, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So are you suggesting the Ozren Tactical Group was also under the command of the forward command post in Lipac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. That forward command post was used to enter Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What do you mean by that, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A temporary command was there that was used to dispatch troops and artillery to their respective positions when Doboj was being occupied in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So wouldn't that post have been under the command of Stankovic, forward command post, a temporary post for the take-over of Doboj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know what we were told. That is, that in Lipac there was a forward command post where orders and commands came from. As to who was there, at the forward command post, is something I cannot say, since I wasn't there. I only know what I had heard. I was cautioned by the Bench not to say what I can't prove.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, if you -- if you don't know, you don't know. Let me return to this, then. You've told us that Stankovic was in charge of the Tactical Group Ozren, and you told us that the Tactical Group Ozren commanded Dragan Lukic, who was the commander of your group. So that means, does it not, that you were commanded by Stankovic, you and your group? Isn't that logically the case and wasn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a very complex issue, in any case. In the course of these few days I will try to get hold of a few documents which will prove the contrary and who commanded what groups. I'm awaiting those documents. Those people who were present, for the most part, were subordinated to Bozovic, and some to Stankovic and to his operations centre and command. Hence, it's a very complex issue for me to be able to explain it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But Stankovic didn't take orders from Bozovic, did he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know whether he did or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And didn't, as you told us a moment ago, regard Bozovic as in charge of the Ozren Tactical Group. Isn't that correct too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bozovic was not at the helm of the Ozren Tactical Group. However, he did have his own group.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But as you told us, you were answerable to the Ozren Tactical Group so you were not part of Bozovic's group, by virtue of what you just said. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the outset, we were. Later on, we were not. Later on, we were answerable to the Ozren Tactical Group, still keeping contact with some people who were under Bozovic though.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Stankovic was responsible, wasn't he, for trying to bring Karaga under control. When Karaga went independent. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One could say that he assisted in bringing him under control. It was a local matter, of the local armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Exactly. And when you were arrested and stayed in Mali Logor for 21 days, you were under Stankovic's detention, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Because there were -- there had been incidents in the territory of Teslic municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And, as you've told us, Stankovic was -- sorry, I don't think you have told us this. Was Stankovic responsible for bringing the Mice group under control? Did he ever do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Stankovic was a close colleague of Minkovic [sic] who was directly commanding the Mice paramilitary group; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Milan Ninkovic, did command the Mice, Mice's group. I'm not certain whether, at that time, Stankovic had already been appointed defence minister of the RS. If he was the defence minister at the time, then he was subordinated to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, I think I asked you the question "Minkovic," and you rightly corrected me and said "Ninkovic," with an N, so that was my error. Thank you. Now, you've told us that Bozovic left the region, I think, in June or July of 1992. Which -- and you've also said in your statements to the Prosecution that, after he left, he continued giving you orders and you suggest he continued giving you orders for many years after that. Can you tell the Court what orders you were given by Bozovic when you were working in these various units under the VRS? I'm asking the question because it's not in your statement. The only order that you -- there was only one order you refer to in your statement. You simply deal with it in a general way and say you were receiving orders from Bozovic. So, please, could you assist the Court and let us know what orders you were receiving from Bozovic? If you want, can you go through the years from 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is difficult for me to recall everything that happened between 1992 and today. We had some contacts with him which were rather intensive until 1997 or 1998, more or less. Even today we still have contact. Well, I don't know whether it is so today, but perhaps until five or six years ago, there were contacts through intermediaries. I can't recall every order, because a lot of time has elapsed, and I can't even recall the events of the time in totality. Unfortunately, time took its toll.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, just give us some orders, a few orders that Bozovic was giving you in your capacity -- as a person working for the VRS.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, I cannot recall. It was a long time ago, and I don't want to say things that I'm uncertain of. I would require some time to recall that. I can't remember everything. It has been 17 years since 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, if you can't recall, then, there is no point in me continuing to ask. Could I suggest you cannot recall because you were not receiving orders from Bozovic after he left the Doboj region? Could that be, really, the basis for your loss of memory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not the reason why. I don't want to speak about things that I'm not 100 per cent certain of. I only speak about things that I'm certain of. As for the rest, that is something I do not wish to address. If I cannot recall things, then it's better for me to say that I cannot than to suggest, speculate or provide wrong information.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. You did -- you have said in your statement that in 1992, after Bozovic left, "he ordered us to expel all the people in a village." Do you recall saying that to the Prosecution? We can turn to it in a minute, if it helps. But I want to ask you if you recall saying that Bozovic ordered you to expel all the people in a particular village?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Paragraph 34 of the first statement, Your Honours, so that Your Honours know where I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you recall giving that evidence to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Bukovicke Civcije.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And what happened to the people who were expelled from that village, according to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were put on buses --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- and transferred to the Federation. Although, by that time, it still had not existed. In any case, they were transferred to the Muslim-held territory. Whereas some of them were separated from the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Who were separated from the rest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Able-bodied men, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. Sorry, what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some ended up in the collection centre at Usora. And some ended -- well, I can only tell you what I had heard from others. Although I do not wish to speak of things that I have no specific proof or information to confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: How did you receive those orders from Bozovic, and what was the nature of the order that you received? Let's just deal with the first bit. How did you receive the orders from Bozovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was issued collectively to us. The platoon commanders went to see him, to the command centre, where they received their orders, and then in the field we implemented them, the orders that had been given to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But this was after Bozovic had left, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that was before that. There were many operations which took place before that, because the loyalty oath was a topical issue at the time, the loyalty oath required by the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So who were you working for at the time this happened then? At what stage was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that stage, I was still with the Special Purpose Unit, although we still kept receiving orders from different groups. It is a confusing issue which I cannot explain, but there were orders coming from the -- both the police system and the military system, depending on the needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I ask, please, for the -- for Exhibit 137 -- P137, please, to come onto the screen, and paragraph 34 of the B/C/S, please. Paragraph, please, 34.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can you have a look at the first sentence, please. "In 1992, after Radojica Bozovic left, he ordered us to expel all the people in the village Bukovicke Civcije." Does it say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does. That's when Operation Corridor began, when there was an attack from Bukovicke Civcije at the police check-point, which was in the outskirts of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And didn't you say earlier today that you were receiving orders from Djuro Martic during corridor operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time, at the time of Operation Corridor, depending on the position one was, that's where orders came from. We received orders from different sides. At the time, and in that location, where the police check-point was, there were so many soldiers that at a certain point in time, people simply didn't know who was asking for what and who wanted what to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Or who was present. Isn't it right that you told the Prosecution that Bozovic had left at the time that this operation to expel the people in this village took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During Operation Corridor he could not have left, because the corridor had not been opened. I think that operation began ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you tell the Prosecution that? Is that the explanation for why it appears in your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There must be a mistake in the statement, because I also had certain other corrections which I made known to the Prosecutor. I even think we discussed this particular paragraph, paragraph 34. There was a number of things which were not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, that's right. I'll come to that. You also, I suggest, told the Prosecution, at the time of your 2004 statement, that the killings related to this crime had taken place at Ozren, as paragraph 34 states. Did you tell the Prosecution that in 2004?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't put it that way. I tried to correct that and we do have a correction of paragraph 34 on record.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... right, Mr. Witness, your correction is -- it's at --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit 138 -- P138, and it's at paragraph 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And now, five or six years later, you say that the killings took place at the Usora camp. Is that your correction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I think -- I'm just objecting on -- on -- there seems to be misquoting from the -- from the statement. I think there's nothing that suggests that the witness says the killings took place at Usora camp in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, you're right. I apologise. I should have put it differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The correction was that the people that were killed at Mount Ozren were detainees from the Usora camp; is that right? Is that the substance of your correction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The gist of my correction was that they had been detainees at the collection centre in Usora.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, I want to move to a different subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Please, I could I have Exhibit P144 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I want to move quickly, please, Mr. Witness, and point out certain things to you and ask you if you have any evidence to give. Can you see the name on the top right of the document? This is a questionnaire relating to Slobodan Vukasin Katanic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Please, if you'd make a mental note of the name Vukasin. We turn over, please, to page 3, and I want to have a look at the information on wounding and treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now can we go to page ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can you see the title "Information on Wounding and Treatment"? Do you see that? No?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can we turn to page 3, please, of the B/C/S. It may not be page 3 then. It's page 3 of the English version, and it ... yes, okay. There it is, I saw it then on the left-hand screen, in English. Could we find the equivalent page, please, of the B/C/S with the -- I'm looking for the title "Information on Wounding and Treatment."

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Is it there on the screen, Mr. Witness? Can you help us out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And it says on the left-hand column: Date and place of enlistment, name of the unit, commander's name and rank, duty in the unit and rank. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could the document please be enlarged so that I can read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think from what my Serbian colleagues say, it may be the next page of the B/C/S. No, it's there. Thank you. Okay. It's the top left-hand of the screen, please, Mr. Witness. Date and place of enlistment, name of the unit, commander's name and rank, duty in the unit and rank; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. Poorly, but I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can you read out, please, the column to the right of that which gives the detail of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, do we have the corresponding English page in front of us?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't think we do. Can we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Take care that we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can we go, please, to page 3 of the English version. Oh, sorry, it is page 3, just further -- no, it's not, it's page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: If I may assist, I think it's at the bottom of page 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: All right. Can you see that, Mr. Witness? I want you to read, please, the -- what it says in the box entitled -- with date and place of enlistment, name of the unit, and so on. What does it say to the right of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says: The 1st of May, in Doboj, Special Police. I can't see what the next word is. Then in the second line: Police, Petrovo. And then I can't say what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... be moved to the left of the screen slightly, please. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Try again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't. We would have to zoom in. I have difficulty reading it. Otherwise, I can't see it clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and then perhaps I'll read it and we can shorten things, because I'm running out of time. Does it say --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now can I see it, I can read it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 1st of May in Doboj, Special Police, special -- then I can't say what it says. Police, Petrovo, Black Berets, Special Purposes Unit, Radojica Bozovic, Lieutenant, and then the last line, Deputy Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So could I suggest to that you Slobodan Vukasin Katanic was a deputy -- the deputy to Bozovic when Bozovic was in Doboj? Could that be the Vuk you refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible. I only told you what I knew; whereas, we were not supposed to ask much. Most of the people I knew, I knew by their first name or nickname. I don't know too many last names. As far as I know -- well, I really don't know what to say about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I suggest you do know that it was this man and he was a local man who worked in the secondary school at -- had previously worked as a teacher in the Brcko locality. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that he used to be a teacher in the municipality of Doboj or in Doboj itself? I can't see it clearly in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I'm -- I'm going on what the document says, which -- at page -- just above where we've just been looking. It says that at some point he worked in the secondary school Vaso Pelagic in Brcko. [Microphone not activated] -- this page. It might be the previous page on the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really don't know who worked as a teacher in Brcko in the school, because here it says he worked in Brcko. I don't know that I ever mentioned that I have ever been in any school in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can I please ask for Exhibit P145, please. The page I'm ... the page I'm interested in, please, is page 5 of the English. The same section, information on wounding and medical treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can you see -- can you see that, Mr. Witness? Can you see the right-hand box again, 3rd of May, 1992, Bosansko Petrovo Selo, Red Berets, currently Special Purposes Battalion, Bozovic. Does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, can I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Does that ring a belt that Bozovic was the commander of units based in Petrovo Selo, Bosansko Petrovo Selo, known as the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, but you said that he was the commander of the unit - let me see if I can quote that correctly - Petrovo police for special purposes. And here it says: Bosansko Petrovo Selo, and I'm quoting you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I ask, please, that we pull up on e-court Defence document 1D91. And the ERN is 04154405. And whilst that is being found, the front page of this document that's coming onto e-court was not in our system for some reason so it hasn't been uploaded. It -- and we haven't provided a draft English translation. So with Your Honours' leave, I will hand a copy to the witness and ask him to read it and confirm it. We've given a copy to the Prosecution to confirm. And we have copies for Your Honours, although it's, as I say, in B/C/S. It's a one-page document. Whilst that is happening, perhaps ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can you see that, Mr. Witness? Would you mind just reading that out, please. The front of the page, what does it say across the middle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it is not very clear. I can only recognise the centre -- Security Services Centre Petrovo in ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can I -- perhaps I shall move on to another subject until this can be found and what I might do is simply ask for this to be tendered since the witness -- it concerns Katanic, Slobodan and the witness has indicated he doesn't -- here it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You want to tender this. What is this, at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, yes. It's -- if I may just quickly refer to a page and then I would like to tender the heading, the front of the page and the document up on the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can you see the name Katanic, Slobodan. This is a document which purports to be from this Republika Srpska MUP, sent to Security Service Doboj, to the ministry, to the MUP Republika Srpska Sarajevo, dated the 1st of September, 1992. Are you following me, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the section that is relevant at the moment is number one, referring to Katanic, Slobodan, son of Vukasin, from Petrovo, born in 1958, professor of physical culture. He has worked as the professor in Brcko. Later he was engaged to be the commander to train special units in Ozren. He is now the commander of reserve police in SJB Petrovo. Does any of that ring a bell to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, from what I know, this does seem familiar but I can't really confirm. But I have to say, it doesn't say here Special Purpose Unit. It still says Special Police, which is really undefined, just like I said earlier. There is a bit of a misunderstanding here about the name. I'm not sure, maybe I'm mistaken. Maybe this is misplaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I will ask for this to be tendered, Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that we have it MFI'd until we have a translation of the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, do I understand you well, that your suggestion is that the Katanic, Slobodan, which is mentioned here is the same as in the questionnaire?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that is the inference we will ask you to draw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That despite the fact that the year of birth differs two years?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We're not suggesting that these documents are accurate. For example, with the Black Beret on the last document, there are mistakes throughout them, we will submit, and the date of birth, we submit, is one of those mistakes. The profession --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which one is the mistake?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We don't know. One of them. But given the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But wouldn't it be appropriate that if you suggest that these are the same persons, that you at least share with the Chamber apparent inconsistencies with the documents; or do you expect the Chamber to go through them in full detail and then find out themselves what are the matters which we need to pay specific attention to.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I thought that that would be subject to argument later on from the Prosecution. It's our submission that they are the same person. That the profession is the same, that the role commanding special units is the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would say you focus on what is consistent and the Chamber will need to take a further look at it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But we first assign a number so that the document will then be assigned.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D13, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. And you can inform the Chamber once a translation has been uploaded, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Witness, you claim to have worked for the JSO. Do you receive a pension from the JSO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now, you mean? No, no, I don't receive a pension.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You claim to have been present during the ceremony at Kula. But did you see yourself on the screen at any point in that ceremony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't see my own image, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You claim that you have a plaque awarded to you for your loyal service, awarded from the Serbian DB. Where is it? (redacted). But that is not a plaque, really, it's just a paper which is a thank-you note, sort of. I believe that it was actually issued to everyone. I think it was just for formality purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Could we please quickly go into closed session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Have you told the Prosecution about this piece of paper, this -- which would prove or go somewhere to proving your ex-status?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember whether I told them about it, but I will try to obtain it as soon as possible and that will confirm my ex-status.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Why haven't you tried so far, given you were going to give evidence in this court, and that, as far as I can see, is the only independent proof that you have produced of your status or that could you produce?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, probably because it never occurred to me to do that, and I didn't look for it. And during my interview with the Prosecution, it never occurred to me that this is something that I could present to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You'll be able to send it to the Prosecution after you have given evidence, will you, so that they can use it to establish who you are? Is that something you can do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, finally, Mr. Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the best is the communication to go through VWS so that it reaches us and that it will be disclosed to both parties. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I want to ask you finally about one subject, Mr. Witness, and it's Exhibit P137, and it's paragraph 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can we have both the English and B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Paragraph 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can we have ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Paragraph 9. And it says at the beginning: "I first learned that we were members of the Serbian DB in 1995. We had been told that we were a JNA special unit." Did you say that in 2004?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. In fact, I did say -- say it, but not in so many words. Because, at the time, as far as I know, the JNA did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, did you say that you first learned that you were members of the Serbian DB in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not hear that we were members of the Serbian DB in 1995, but, rather, that the unit that had trained us, in fact, had its roots in the DB, in the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I suggest that you have not ever seen an order from Jovica Stanisic concerning the events in Doboj, as you have, in 2009, claimed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you can claim whatever you please. But I know what I saw. It's the same with you claiming that there was this unit of the Special Police in Petrovo Selo, whereas documents point to something else. And from the documents that I have proposed to hand over to the Trial Chamber, I believe that other things can be seen as well, and then we can claim, or disclaim, whether I did or did not see things.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, you didn't mention seeing orders from Stanisic when you were first interviewed in 2004, did you? Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I didn't say I remember there was a name, whether this was an order or there was just a sheet of paper which was headed "Information." I don't know, because too much time has passed, and I need more time in order to obtain all those documents that could prove that. Because many documents have been destroyed and others have been misplaced so you actually have to go searching for documents one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can you try to keep your answer to the question. The first time you mentioned Stanisic and orders or seeing orders from Stanisic was in 2008 or 2009, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not so. I actually saw a piece of paper and I assume -- now whether these were orders or not, I don't know. But there was his name there, as far as I can recall. But I'm not sure. I assume that it was his name on that piece of paper, as far as can I recall, but I cannot be 100 per cent certain. In other words, whether I saw an order with which I never had any context, so I couldn't claim that, but -- and seeing a piece of paper and a name on it, I could have seen that, and I remember that there was mention made of that name. So can I claim that with certainty. Yes, I did see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So you saw a piece of paper with a name on it and you assumed that it was Stanisic. Is that what you just said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I saw the name, the first and last name, that sounds like this name, and I'm sure that that was a similar name, and what the context of that document was, I really don't know. And as I said, I can't recall it, because many years -- 17 years have passed. But I will try to get hold of that paper, and if I do, I will forward it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Looking at the last two minutes, I see that there's a bit confusion on when something was first mentioned and what the witness recalls. Let's try to clearly separate that. I mean, the matter started with: What did you say in 2004; I suggest that it was for the first time in 2008, 2009, that you saw this -- a repetitious mixing up of first mentioning a certain matter and what the -- what the witness remembered, either in 2004, or in 2008, or now. I just want to put that on the record, that there's a -- creating at least some confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, let me just ... You have not mentioned -- you didn't mention to the Prosecution anything about seeing pieces of paper with Stanisic's name on it until 2008 or 2009, did you? You didn't make mention of it in your 2004 statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you know what 17 years mean? I can remember some things but others I can't. But, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the truth is that what happened was that you heard rumours during your time in Doboj that the Serbian DB was involved; and it was just that, rumours, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, all right, if that's what you're claiming. Although that would not be my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And paragraph 9 of the exhibit, P137, where you say: "We heard rumours about it before that ..." Before 1995, was the truthful account. It was rumours, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, now, again, before that, is before 1995. Let's be clear what is statement given 2004, what is later statements what we hear today, and if to say, you heard about this rumours, that's clearly in the context to be understood as that before he learned as -- at least the statement reads he learned something in 1995, that prior to that, he was aware of rumours. Let's try to get things chronologically, what happened when. This is prior to learning something in 1995. That's at least how the statement reads. And if you put the statement to the witness, then it should be -- it should clarify rather than confuse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I ask for a break, Your Honour -- may I ask for a break? I'm actually feeling really unwell and a break would do me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- apart from -- Mr. Jordash, I'm sorry that you do not feel well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And apart from that, it is for your client we would have sessions of 75 minutes so I was about to see when you would stop. We'll have a break, and we will resume at ten minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was wondering with Your Honours leave, I could stop now and leave the matter of clarification to my learned friend for Mr. Simatovic. If -- I could then come back to it, if Your Honour is not satisfied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand, therefore, that do you not feel well yet. This is agreeable so that Mr. Knoops will be here with us when the cross-examination by the Simatovic Defence will be conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, I remain for a while and see how I go, but later on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We leave it to you, and if it causes insurmountable problems then, of course, the Chamber would like to be informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This, then, means that this, as matters stand now, concludes the examination-in-chief -- the cross-examination by the Stanisic Defence. Who is it, Mr. Bakrac, will it be you, or will it be Mr. Petrovic who cross-examines the witness? Apparently Mr. Petrovic. Witness JF-005, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Petrovic is counsel for Mr. Simatovic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. I will have a few questions to put to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we first and foremost move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Petrovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell us, just in a few sentence, could you describe the camp at Ozren where you went for training? Just in a few words, how many buildings, and what it looked like. Be brief.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where we were accommodated there was a building, and we were trained in the use of weapons --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting. All I'm asking you about is what the camp itself looked like. I'm not asking about the training that you were put through.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was a facility there - I think the building had about three to four floors - where we were accommodated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What type of facility was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what purposes it served before that. Later on, I heard that it was used as a tourist hotel or a hostel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And you were accommodated there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a number of us were accommodated there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, my question is about you yourself. So you said that you yourself were accommodated and slept in this building, which had two or three floors, as you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, how many buildings were there in that -- on that site?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there were, I believe, three buildings. One of them was larger and the other two were smaller buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And you had your quarters in this larger building; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What was -- what were the two other -- the smaller buildings, what purpose did they serve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, one of them was a weapons depot of sorts. We left our weapons there. And as for the third building, I really didn't know what it was, nor were there any men accommodated there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So, in other words, you would leave your weapons at the depot once you returned from training.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We had our weapons with us all the time, but the additional weapons that we received, we would leave it at the depot. It was a sort of warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Could you now tell us, please, where was Bozovic accommodated? Where were his sleeping quarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know where because he wasn't with us, so I can't really say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But do you know where his offices were, where some sort of command was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, at that time, no, I don't know where the headquarters were. We underwent training there. We went through various courses. I don't know where his offices were. And later on, we had dealings and we had training at the Ministry of Defence in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please just answer my questions. And please also make pauses between question and answer, and answer and question, and let's be careful not to overlap so that everyone can do their job. So you do not know where Bozovic's headquarters were or his command was. Did you have any kind of pass?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What kind of pass was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had a sort of temporary ID or pass which we could use to move freely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking about a pass to this camp itself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we didn't have any kind of pass for the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In two words, could you describe what the training consisted of, in one -- on any given day, how did it begin and how did it start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in the morning, when we get up, we would go running. Then we had tactical training. We used our weapons. So that's what a typical day would look like.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what type of skills were you trained in and did you learn at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the most important skill that I learned was topography, but I can't tell you what it was that I really liked, what type of training at the time, but we had topography. We had combat skills and especially --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the last words that the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his last words which were not caught by the interpreter. You said: But I can't tell you -- I can't tell what you -- it is with a that I really liked what. Could you please repeat those -- the last part of your sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. Well, I said mines and explosives, explosive devices.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please tell us, the mine and explosive devices, talking about that, what exactly did you learn? How were you to handle those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we learned how to mount and defuse mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell us, please, could you say something about the discipline at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was very strict. And in my view, that was correct, and that's -- that was proper, and that's how discipline should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I suppose that you -- when you -- as you went through training, no one ever instructed you to commit war crimes or anything similar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, quite the contrary. We were taught how to properly use our weapons. So, yes, I can say that nobody ever taught us or instructed us to commit any crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please tell us, you said that the discipline was very strict, that the regime was rigorous. I assume that for all of you who attended this course, you were not really in a position to socialise with Bozovic, to meet with him in some sort of informal setting, have a drink or so on. I suppose that was really not an option.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that wasn't an option, and I -- I never actually was present or ever witnessed anything like that. So, no, that couldn't -- that was out of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I can further deduce from what you said that you were not really in a position to monitor Bozovic's activities, who he met, whom he had contacts with, and exchanged information. So just tell us about what you know and if you ever heard of anything. So just what you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right. Well, me personally, I was not in a position to monitor Bozovic's activities, nor could I ever see or observe what -- or from whom he received any communications or dispatches.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, then, please, how it is that in your statement - and that's document P137 - you state the following, and I'm referring to paragraph 41: "I often heard Rajo Bozovic speaking with people from Belgrade when he stayed in Doboj and he often addressed them using the polite form. I know it was Belgrade because I saw the number that he dialed." So is this incorrectly noted here as to what you could remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is correct. I could see the number that he was dialing, and I wasn't the only one because we were all concerned about what would happen with the local population.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, please, you tell us about yourself. When and where did you see Rajo Bozovic dialing a number in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the police staying in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the counsel. The microphone was off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, your microphone was off when you did put the question. Would you please repeat it so that it can be interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question was: What was the number that he dialled? And the witness understood my question in B/C/S, so he replied. And my question was: What the number that he dialled?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then we would like to hear the answer. Could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. I saw that he dialled a number beginning with 011, but I can't recall the number. I remember, because this area code, 011, was the area code for Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But a few moments ago, you told us you weren't in a position to see ever who it was that Bozovic called or had contacts with and how he communicated. You just said so two minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know who it was that he called and who -- whom he contacted, and I couldn't hear the other side answering or talking. So I observed this only in passing. I don't know whom he talked with, but I did see the area code that he dialled. But as for who it was that he called, I really don't know. I didn't see, nor do I have any information.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe it was a private call, a private phone call.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's possible. That is why I stressed here that he used the polite form.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, you spent 12 days in training there, correct, in total?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We had some 15 days of training, and then a few additional days. And then, later on, we underwent some training just as we went, in passing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't understand your statement. You say that on the 20th of April your training began, and that on the 3rd of May already, the attack on Doboj was launched.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct. That was about 13 days. Then we went down from Mount Ozren, we descended, and then there were a couple of additional days that we underwent training on. I believe this was while we were in Ozren. And then on 5th and 6th of May, on the 6th of May, the mopping-up operation began.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you about your training. You said that your training began on the 23rd and it ended on the 3rd.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it began on 23rd but it didn't end on the 3rd. We -- on the 3rd we were sent to an assignment. We were supposed to man check-points, and then we returned back to Ozren and then spent two or three more days to complete our train.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, may I also invite you to not only ask the witness to make the pauses but make them yourself as well. Mr. Hoffmann, you were on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would ask that we please go quickly into closed session once more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unless, Mr. Petrovic, you think we should stay for a while in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please remain in private session so that we can clarify this. And I apologise if I inadvertently caused something to be disclosed, but I would appreciate it if we remained in closed -- in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We remain in private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would just like to remind you. My question to you was: Was -- did the person you saw then have short hair, and that was on page 57, line 2. And I believe that your answer was yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, what do you mean by "short hair"? It could be two or five, six centimetres long. If you say -- when I think of long hair, I mean long hair.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The counsel did not turn on his microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters tell us that you had not turned on your microphone in the last question, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. The error is mine. But I am trying to make sure that the witness's voice would not be heard. But he tries to answer -- he is quick in his answers, and that is the reason why I failed to actually turn on the microphone at the very same moment when my colleague begins speaking. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The last question to the witness was: Did this person that the witness had seen, did he look like Simatovic, as we see him here today? Could the witness please give his answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he does look like him. I can't say it is his him. But he does look like him and he did have -- his hair was a bit longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In 1995, you said that you were in Fruska Gora. Could you tell us where in Fruska Gora were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were stationed, I can't remember exactly the site, but we were quartered in a building where we spent some two or three days and then we went back. Because, in those days, there was an issue about people who hailed from Bosnia and Herzegovina. They were actually pressured to go back, to return to their units, so I can't recall. But it was close to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall what town or what village this was in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, no, I really have difficulty remembering place names.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what this building looked like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was just a house where we were accommodated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please tell us something about Teslic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What do you know about the events in Teslic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I'll start from the beginning. Would you want me to start from the beginning, from the first moment when we received the information and then on?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well -- please tell us what about what you know, what happened there and what was going on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, there was Karaga's group, in Teslic, and they were actually expelling the non-Serb population, but then a problem arose when they began taking valuables from the Serbs in the area.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the counsel's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness JF-005, if counsel makes a pause in order to put his next question to you, then it's better to wait for his next question rather than to continue your answer after a moment of silence. Your next question was, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How long -- how much time did Karaga's group spend in Teslic? How long did they stay there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, and as far as we knew, they were there up to seven days prior to our arrival in Teslic. As far as I can recall. It's possible that they stayed there longer, but I don't have any information to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Ljubisa Trcivic [phoen] is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It sounds familiar but I can't tell you off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Dobrivoje Culibrk [Realtime transcript read in error "Dobriboj Tulovic"] is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That, too, sounds familiar. I can't recall off the cuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Milan Savic is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That name does not sounds familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I asked the witness, on page 60, line 11, I asked him if he knew the name -- who Dobrivoje Culibrk is, and I assume that this will be corrected in the transcript later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know any of these men. Do you know who Ranko Sljuka is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Rodoljub Sljivic is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the last two men, Sljivic and Sljuka, were in Teslic at the time in question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. But I do know that they were members of the Mice, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who called Karaga to Teslic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that Dobrivoje Culibrk, Deputy Chief of the National Security Service in Doboj, invited Karaga to Teslic, would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please just repeat the function that he was on?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The Deputy Chief of National Security Service in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: State Security or National Security?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, national or state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, are we now in open or closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: We are in open session but it is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as far as I recall, if I'm not mistaken, Marko Mihetic [phoen] was the Deputy Chief of State Security, and he was in charge of sector 2, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: My question to you was: Is it possible, do you allow for the possibility that Culibrk was actually the person who invited Karaga to Teslic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who did you go with to Teslic? Who was in the group, together with you, who went to Teslic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, there were four or five of us in the group. That was the standard composition of the group.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please move to private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Mr. Petrovic, I'm looking at the clock. We had another session of a little bit over 75 minutes. Therefore, I'd rather first have the break. Mr. Petrovic, could you give us an indication as to how much more time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is difficult to give you an exact estimate, but we will probably need an extra half-hour tomorrow during the first session, and I hope that would be it. And I will try to trim down my questions as much as I can. Of course, if you allow me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which would mean that you would need another one hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, the next witness takes how much time in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The witness will take an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: An hour and a half. How much time would you need for the cross-examination of the next witness? Mr. Knoops, perhaps you ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Approximately half an hour, 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Half an hour, 40 minutes. And the --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same, Your Honours. Not more than 30 to 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under those circumstances, and having looked at the -- the next witness will be viva voce, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Half an hour, 40 minutes would be half of a session. One hour and a half for the Prosecution; then 30 to 40 minutes would be half a session. 30 to 40 minutes, that would be, all together, approximately two sessions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, you are invited to focus on the most important issues. We'll then see how that develops. Level of relevance, importance, will then be assessed by the Chamber. You're urged to see whether you can reorganise your cross-examination in such a way that we could finish today. We will consider whether we'll grant you some additional time, and that would certainly not be more than half an hour, if any time at all. So, therefore, you're invited to -- to achieve this. As matters stand now, will there be a lot of re-examination, Mr. Hoffmann?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would not expect more than, maybe ten or 15 minutes at the -- at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which, added to the time -- what we want to avoid is that either this witness or the next witness has to remain for many, many days for just a very small portion. And the Chamber considers that it should be possible, in view of the subject matter, the way in which the examination takes place until now, that we would be able to finish -- to conclude the testimony of this witness and the next witness together by tomorrow, the end of the session. Again -- and I emphasise that it is always difficult to know exactly what the witness is going to say, but, at least, Mr. Petrovic, you'll save some time by switching on your microphone and but not putting a question which you then have to repeat because you started that question before the translation of the previous answer was given by the interpreters. We'll have a break, and we will resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may, I need a moment of your time, and it may be of assistance in your ruling concerning the witness for tomorrow. We checked it with our client, and I don't think I'll need more than 30 minutes for the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that information, Mr. Bakrac. Yes, we do not save a lot, but you said 30 to 45 minutes, but, okay, we now know that at least it's 30 and not 45. Mr. Petrovic, are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am, Your Honour. Thank you. Let's move into private session, please, to complete our discussion we began just before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Your microphone was not activated. But I heard you say: "We're in open session, Your Honours." That's on the record. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I asked you about the camp at Tara. What do you know about it; where is that -- where was that camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were brought to a spot not far from Bajina Basta. We stayed in the woods where there was a virtual, let's call it that, training centre. I can't tell you for certain who this camp belonged to or who it was run by. I couldn't really say. We didn't see any of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last answer, because it wasn't clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was in 1995 or 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last portion of your last answer. I'll start reading: "I can't tell you for certain who this camp belonged to or who it was run by. I couldn't really say. We didn't see" -- And then what were your remaining words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't see any of the people who had been with us earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How many training camps were there on Mount Tara and on the banks of the river Tara?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really don't know what the number was or how many of them there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you only know of this one camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, where we were billeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Near Bajina Basta?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, not far from Bajina Basta.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It looked like the camp at Rijecani. It was similar. There were tents, and I'm mentioning Rijecani because it was similar to this camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please tell me ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last question was missed by the interpreter. Now, I take it that you asked him to describe the one camp the witness talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But could you -- could you please make that little pause, which avoids that we have to intervene again and again. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. But because of the time constraints, I'm trying to be as efficient as possible and to save as much time as I can, but I will do my best to make the pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, all you know about Tara is that one camp with tents that you've described.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, then, how it is that in your statement - and you said that you have read it carefully - your 1999 statement, P138, reads as follows, and that's in paragraph 22. P138: "The camp at the Tara river consisted of three different sites. Half of them were in Serbia, close to BH and Montenegro, and the other half was in Montenegro." How did this find way into your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that was the explanation that we were given at the camp, that there were other locations, but I only mentioned the one that I knew of.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You were sent -- you were sent for some special training somewhere. Who sent you where and when? Could you please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What special training are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, it says in your statement here that you were trained for computer literacy. What kind of training was this, what kinds of course was this and who sent you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were then with this man I knew well, Rajo Bozovic, who sent there -- who was with Rajo Bozovic, who sent us there to be trained in computers, and I received a certificate at the end of this course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So if I understood you properly, you knew a man --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know a man. I was -- there was a man who was with him and who told us that in his conversation with Bozovic this is what he was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What exactly was he told?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that we should report at the RRK Informatika, and that we will attend a type of course there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What was the name of the person who told you that, or do you want to us move to private session?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, if you want me to tell you the name, please, let's move to private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please move to private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why were you sent to attend this course, this computer course, and what does that have to do with your overall involvement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I just know that I completed this course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where did you attend this course?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At RRK Informatika.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where exactly; can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
