utterances.text: I don't know the street name. Just a moment, I'll try to recall the name. I can't remember the street address. I knew it, but I can't recall it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What part of the city was it in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between Dorcol and -- in that area, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What did you learn at that course?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, try and tell us some of it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the use of Office. Then the ability to create programmes in the COBOL language and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was this a private school that you attended?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you, really. We did have private classes, but I can't really say with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any pay in the course of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We were remunerated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, for the most part, we received cash.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where was it paid out to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that would depend. From/to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, where were you given this money? Would someone bring it to you at home, or in Informatika?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the most part we were paid out at Doboj or wherever we happened to be. Some people even received money at the Institute for State Security.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you bear with me, I need to check something.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where did you get the money? In Doboj for the most part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not in Doboj. In Belgrade. I just told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where did you receive the money personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Depending on where we were in the course, they would come in the evening to pay us, and some people went to the Institute for State Security.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness JF-005, where did you receive the money?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was explaining you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Once the classes at Dorcol were finished?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In P137, paragraph 43 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. "During the course, I received remuneration from the Serbian Ministry of the Interior in cash. I went to the financial department of the DB to get the money."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you now what I had told at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic's mic was off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Institute for State Security.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were you ever -- Let's try it this way. During the time we're discussing, 1992 to, say, 1999, where was the seat of the State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know where the Institute for State Security was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever go to the seat of the State Security of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where did you go then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the Institute for State Security.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who did you go to see there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a conversation with this person, although I cannot tell you that person's name anymore. But I can tell you how we got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I want to know who you saw in the seat of the State Security. You told me where you went, and now you tell me what office. Who was in that office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall the last name of the person. I was taken there, and I can describe to you where the office is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As you enter the parking lot of the institute, there is a building just in front of the parking lot, and there's one on the side. They're perpendicular to each other. We entered the first one, to the offices on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What you're telling me is from 1995, among other years; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I think it was in 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Before 2000, you never went to any building which would be the seat of the State Security Service or the Institute for State Security?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to other institutions and offices of the state security in the Republika Srpska but not in Serbia itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: After 2000, who did you go there with, to visit the institute?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That person is in direct relation to me, so could we please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic's mic was off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If I understand your question [as interpreted] correctly, before 2000, you were never in the seat of the State Security or at the institute, but you visited some other institutions in the RS.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, I conclude that you don't know where Mr. Simatovic's office was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Or, say, Bozovic's office.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't. I was only told that they were in the building that was before or in front of the parking lot, although I don't know where exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony, you said that, between 1995 and 2001, you were a member of the Special Operations Unit; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were constantly being told that, and all the people who had been there remained with the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. So you're not certain whether you were a member of the Special Operations Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were all as part of a reserve force, if I can call it that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you corroborate what you're saying? Do you have any documents to prove that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could get a hold of a few documents and I would be able to hand it over to the Tribunal in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And the Prosecutor never asked for any such -- such a document which would confirm your participation in that unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Never?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an ID?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I mean the Special Operations Unit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, not for that one. We didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What was your relationship with the unit? Were you kept anywhere? What reflected your status?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What reflected our status? They maintained contact with us, in case we needed to be reactivated. We were all there. They had contact with all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever go to a base of the units for special operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only in Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where did the unit have its other bases?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Belgrade, and I don't know whether anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When did you go to Kula for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's hard to say. 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How many times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: For how long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time around, we were there for a couple of hours. The second time, a bit longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How much longer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four, four and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What did you do the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We just went there to see, with some other active members of the Special Operations Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And the second time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were just invited to a celebration concerning the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it at the same time when President Milosevic was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I presume it was an important event.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was a very important event.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Something difficult to forget, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In 2004, why did you not say to the OTP investigators that you attended such an important ceremony, such as the unit celebration ceremony that they asked you about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not ask me about that on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you a different thing. How is it possible that no one asked you whether you were in Kula or in a base, and when, and on what occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't answer that. You have to put that question to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I will. I'll tell you the following. They did ask you, in para -- it's P137, para 54.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 54, P137. It says: "I was present once while Milosevic was there. It was in 1997. He came to Kula, late in the evening, to have a meeting with Frenki and Jovica Stanisic."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: "They thought Kula was the safest area in the whole of the Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is incorrect. It is wrongly formulated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What exactly is wrong? That's unclear to me. Didn't he come? Didn't he meet with Mr. Stanisic, or Mr. Simatovic? Is Kula not the safest place to meet? What was wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The period when they met is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say it was not in 1997.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It wasn't in the evening. The time of day was wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the year was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When did you see the recording of the ceremony in Kula for the first time, and who showed it to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw parts of the footage before, and the whole footage only here, at the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: My question is: When did you see the footage of the ceremony in Kula for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just told you. I saw parts of it before. I saw the whole footage when I arrived in -- at the Tribunal. The whole footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I put it to you that you changed your statement after having seen the recording; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you tell my learned friend Mr. Hoffmann that you attended the ceremony in 2008?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. In 2008, I was not in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: We're not on the same page. When Mr. Hoffmann discussed this in 2008 with you, did you tell him that you attended a ceremony in Kula?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 2D3 put on the screen. It is a draft statement compiled by Mr. Hoffmann after his interview with this witness in 2008, para 30. Paragraph 30, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: It says: "I was shown a footage of camp Kula from May 1997. I recognise many people appearing on the footage." Is it possible that Mr. Hoffmann, on that occasion, did not take note of your attendance of that ceremony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is possible. Because he showed me the footage and asked me whether I recognised anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And he didn't ask you if you were there, and you didn't tell him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't tell him I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Because he didn't ask you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said I wasn't there and such a question was not put to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When were you asked that for the first time, if you were in Kula? When did Mr. Hoffmann or the other five or six investigators who spoke with you ask you that for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, it is five minutes to 7.00. Could you give us an idea as to where you are because I would like to read a decision as well. But we'll refrain from doing it if you think you could finish and conclude in the next five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot, not in the next five minutes. But I will, indeed, restrict myself to a very short period of time, and I will meet your instructions in full.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would it -- a good guess if I would say that you need another 15 minutes tomorrow? Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do my utmost so that it happens that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I would like to already excuse the witness for today and then read the decision. Witness JF-005, we'd like to see you back tomorrow, quarter past 2.00, in this courtroom. It will not take very long tomorrow. I again instruct you not to speak with anyone, not to, in any other way communicate with anyone, also if you think -- if you think you need to find other material - although, first of all, no one asked for it, and, second, already that material is in the hands of Prosecution - then it would be wiser if you seek through Victims and Witness Section that you seek the approval of the Chamber first, explaining what it is that you so urgently need to ask for. We'd like to see your e-mails tomorrow, as you have told us that -- I think you told us that you would bring them to us. Then could you please follow the usher. You're excused for today, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow, quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would like to read a decision, deliver an oral decision on the Prosecution's motion for protective measures for witnesses filed 6th of January, 2010, and on the Prosecution request for leave to reply to the Stanisic Defence response to the Prosecution motion for protective measures for witnesses filed on the 21st of January, 2010, but only in as far as they relate to Witness B-1048. The Chamber stays its decision on these two motions with regard to Witness B-1459. In its 6 January motion, the Prosecution requests that Witness B-1048 be granted a pseudonym and face distortion (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: (redacted). The Prosecution refers, inter alia, to the most recent report of the Office of the High Representative in Bosnia and Herzegovina, which I from now on will refer to the OHR, to argue that relations between Bosnian Serbs and Bosnian Muslim in the Republika Srpska have worsened in the summer and autumn 2009. If you would excuse me for one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Stanisic Defence in its response of the 20th of January, 2010, argues that Witness B-1048's fears are subjective and that he has not received any specific threats. The Stanisic Defence further contests the Prosecution's reliance on the OHR report which has not been disclosed to the Defence as it would impermissibly lower the threshold for protective measures. The Simatovic Defence did not respond to the motion. In the 21st of January request to reply, the Prosecution states that it seeks to address certain alleged inaccuracies and incorrect assumptions made by the Stanisic Defence. The party seeks protective measures for a witness must demonstrate an objectively grounded risk to the security or welfare of the witness or the witness's family, should it become known that the witness has given evidence before the Tribunal. This standard may be satisfied by showing that a threat was made against the witness, or the witness's family. It may also be met by demonstrating a combination of the following three factors. One, the witness's testimony may antagonise persons who reside in a specific territory; two, the witness or his or her family live or work in that territory, have property in that territory or have concrete plans to return to live in that territory; and three, there exists an unstable security situation in that territory which is particularly unfavorable to witnesses who appear before the Tribunal. We now briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber considers that, in view of the status of the witness and of the subject matter of his testimony, the protective measures requested by the Prosecution, namely, a pseudonym a face distortion, would not guarantee that his security and that of his family are adequately safe-guarded. The Chamber, therefore, orders, pursuant to Article 20, paragraph 1 of the Tribunal's Statute, and Rule 75 of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence, that Witness B-1048 shall be referred to by his pseudonym in all public proceedings and filings, and that he shall testify with the protective measures of closed session. Furthermore, in light of this decision, the Chamber denies the Prosecution request for leave to reply, in as far as it concerns Witness B-1048. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. With apologies for the late conclusion of today's session, we adjourn, and we will resume tomorrow, the 26th of January, quarter past 2.00, Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 26th day of January, 2010, at 2.15 p.m. 25
